data.title: WEBCO INDUSTRIES, INC. REPORTS FISCAL 2026 FOURTH QUARTER AND YEAR END RESULTS
data.description:
WEBCO INDUSTRIES, INC. REPORTS FISCAL 2026 FOURTH QUARTER AND YEAR END RESULTS

WEBCO INDUSTRIES, INC. REPORTS FISCAL 2026 FOURTH QUARTER AND YEAR END RESULTS

PR Newswire

SAND SPRINGS, Okla., Sep 25, 2026

SAND SPRINGS, Okla., Sept. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Webco Industries, Inc. (OTC: WEBC) today reported results for our fourth fiscal quarter and year ended July 31, 2026.

For our fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, we had net income of $5.0 million, or $7.35 per diluted share, while in our fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025, we had net income of $6.5 million, or $9.18 per diluted share. Net sales for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 were $189.7 million, a 19.9 percent increase from the $158.2 million in sales in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025.

For fiscal year 2026, we generated net income of $18.3 million, or $26.50 per diluted share, compared to a net income of $9.3 million, or $12.30 per diluted share, in fiscal year 2025. Net sales for the current fiscal year totaled $670.9 million, a 14.8 percent increase from the $584.7 million in sales for last year.

In the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, we had income from operations of $7.7 million after depreciation of $5.1 million. The fourth fiscal quarter of the prior year generated income from operations of $9.0 million after depreciation of $4.8 million. Gross profit for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 was $27.7 million, or 14.6 percent of net sales, compared to $22.0 million, or 13.9 percent of net sales, for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025.

Our income from operations for fiscal year 2026 was $28.0 million, after depreciation expense of $20.0 million. Income from operations in fiscal year 2025 was $16.6 million, after depreciation expense of $19.0 million. Gross profit for fiscal 2026 was $94.0 million, or 14.0 percent of net sales, compared to $66.8 million, or 11.4 percent of net sales for fiscal year 2025.

Selling, general and administrative expenses were $20.0 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 and $12.9 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025. SG&A expenses were $66.0 million in fiscal year 2026 and $50.2 million for fiscal year 2025. SG&A expenses reflect increases in costs related to higher profitability, such as company-wide incentive compensation and variable pay programs, plus inflation we have experienced in wages and other expenses.

Interest expense was $1.5 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026 and $1.4 million in the same quarter of fiscal year 2025. Interest expense was $5.9 million and $5.3 million in the current and prior fiscal years, respectively. Interest expense increased due to higher average debt balances than in the prior fiscal periods.

Capital expenditures incurred amounted to $1.8 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026 and $15.4 million for fiscal year 2026. Capital spending in fiscal year 2026 has been focused on plant equipment updates and improvements.

At July 31, 2026, we had $9.1 million in cash and short-term investments, in addition to $112.9 million of available borrowing under our $220 million senior revolving credit facility. Availability on the revolver, which had $89.3 million drawn at July 31, 2026, is subject to advance rates on eligible accounts receivable and inventories. In February 2026, we extended the maturity on our debt agreement to February 2031. Accounting rules require asset-based debt agreements like our revolver to be classified as a current liability, despite its fiscal year 2031 maturity.

Webco's stock repurchase program authorizes the purchase of our outstanding common stock in private or open market transactions. In March 2026, the Company's Board of Directors refreshed the repurchase program with a new limit of up to $6.0 million and extended the program's expiration until July 31, 2029. We purchased 11,900 shares of our stock during the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026 and 33,800 shares in fiscal year 2026. At July 31, 2026, there was approximately $1.6 million of purchase authority left in the current stock repurchase program. The repurchase plan may be extended, suspended or discontinued at any time, without notice, at the Board's discretion. 

Webco's mission is to continuously build on our strengths as we create a vibrant company for the ages. We leverage our core values of trust and teamwork, continuously building strength, agility and innovation. We focus on practices that support our brand such that we are 100% engaged every day to build a forever kind of company for our Trusted Teammates, customers, business partners, investors and community. We provide high-quality carbon steel, stainless steel and other metal specialty tubing products designed to industry and customer specifications. We have five tube production facilities in Oklahoma and Pennsylvania and eight value-added facilities in Oklahoma, Illinois, Michigan, Pennsylvania and Texas, serving customers globally. Our F. William Weber Leadership Campus is in Sand Springs, Oklahoma and houses our corporate offices and our Webco TechCenter™, providing a state-of-the-art laboratory and R & D facility to lead and develop technical solutions for the metal tubing industry.

Such forward-looking statements involve known and unknown risks, uncertainties and other important factors that could cause the actual results, performance or achievements of the Company, or industry results, to differ materially from any future results, performance or achievements expressed or implied herein. Such risks, uncertainties and factors include the factors discussed above and, among others: general economic and business conditions, including any global economic downturn; government policy or low hydrocarbon prices that stifle domestic investment in energy; global or regional wars and conflicts; our inability or unwillingness to comply with rules required to maintain the quotation of our shares on any market place; and our inability to repurchase the Company's stock. data.title: $58 Million Multifamily Asset Sale Closed by Institutional Property Advisors in North Phoenix
data.description:
$58 Million Multifamily Asset Sale Closed by Institutional Property Advisors in North Phoenix

Institutional Property Advisors (IPA), a division of Marcus & Millichap (NYSE:MMI) dedicated to serving the company’s institutional clients, announced today the sale of Ascend at Black Canyon, a 260-unit multifamily property in Phoenix, Arizona. The asset traded for $58.7 million, or $225,769 per unit.

“North Phoenix is positioned to generate tens of thousands of high-earning jobs supporting the world’s most advanced nanometer chip production for companies such as Apple, Sony, Tesla, and Qualcomm,” said Steve Gebing, IPA executive managing director investments. “Within a one-mile radius of Ascend at Black Canyon, average and median annual household incomes are $163,500 and $138,000, respectively.” Gebing and Cliff David, IPA executive managing director investments, represented the seller, D.R. Horton, and procured the buyer, Millburn & Company.

The property is in Phoenix’s Deer Valley urban village close to Interstate 17/Black Canyon Freeway, near the Sonoran Preserve and the Happy Valley Town Center open-air shopping mall. Nearby employers include HonorHealth Sonoran Crossing Medical Center, PetSmart’s corporate headquarters, Honeywell Aerospace, Cox Communications, and American Express.

Completed on over 10 acres in 2024, Ascend at Black Canyon is a controlled-access community with a resort-style swimming pool, 24-hour fitness center, two dog parks and a pet washing station. The unit mix is one-, two- and three-bedroom apartments with stainless-steel appliances, washers and dryers, smart-home technology, dual-pane windows and a private patio or balcony.

About Institutional Property Advisors (IPA)

Institutional Property Advisors (IPA) is a division of Marcus & Millichap (NYSE: MMI), a leading commercial real estate services firm in North America. IPA’s combination of real estate investment and capital markets expertise, industry-leading technology, and acclaimed research offers customized solutions for the acquisition, disposition and financing of institutional properties and portfolios. For more information, please visit www.institutionalpropertyadvisors.com.

About Marcus & Millichap, Inc. (NYSE: MMI)

Marcus & Millichap, Inc. is a leading brokerage firm specializing in commercial real estate investment sales, financing, research and advisory services with offices throughout the United States and Canada. Marcus & Millichap closed 8,818 transactions with a sales volume of $50.8 billion in 2025. The company had 1,808 investment sales and financing professionals in more than 80 offices who provide investment brokerage and financing services to sellers and buyers of commercial real estate at year end. For additional information, please visit www.MarcusMillichap.com.

Gina Relva, VP of Public Relations

data.title: MagLev Aero Secures Dual DARPA Contracts to Advance Next-Generation U.S. Drone Propulsion
data.description:
MagLev Aero Secures Dual DARPA Contracts to Advance Next-Generation U.S. Drone Propulsion

MagLev Aero Secures Dual DARPA Contracts to Advance Next-Generation U.S. Drone Propulsion

PR Newswire

BOSTON, Sept. 25, 2026

Concurrent DARPA awards provide non-dilutive funding to accelerate MagLev Aero's path to TRL-6 flight readiness, de-risking dual-use commercialization and advancing U.S.-manufactured propulsion for American "Drone Dominance" initiatives.

BOSTON, Sept. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Propulsion has always been at the core of aircraft performance. As defense drones undergo a rapid performance escalation on the modern battlefield, there remains a critical, unmet need for advanced propulsion systems capable of establishing true drone air dominance. Addressing this challenge, MagLev Aero, a pioneer in advanced aerospace propulsion technology, today announced it has been selected by the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) for concurrent awards under the Minimum Viable Product (MVP) and Embedded Entrepreneur Initiative (EEI) programs.

MagLev Aero has created a breakthrough in propulsion technology that provides more thrust for less power, fundamentally changing the physics of flight. This highly efficient architecture directly enables higher speeds, longer operational ranges, increased payload capacities, and a dramatically reduced noise signature—all the key domains required for drones that must evade detection and capture, counter-drones designed to catch and kill hostile threats, and cargo drones for contested logistics.

Supported by this non-dilutive government funding and an accelerating defense-market demand signal, MagLev Aero is advancing the industrialization of its next-generation propulsion platform. The platform is purpose-built to meet the surging demand for high-performance, U.S.-manufactured drone propulsion, aligning directly with White House "Drone Dominance" priorities, and the rapidly expanding commercial advanced air mobility (AAM) market. DARPA funding will support rapid advancement from prototype to flight-tested production, significantly reducing technical and integration risks for dual-use commercialization.

DARPA MVP - Accelerating Flight Readiness for Airframers
DARPA's MVP support helps technology developers quickly prototype, test, and adapt breakthroughs. MagLev Aero is funded to build and test a full-scale, flight-relevant propulsion demonstration platform, culminating in a Technology Readiness Level 6 (TRL-6) demonstration in a relevant operational environment. This effort significantly de-risks adoption for airframers and OEMs developing the next generation of autonomous drones and crewed aircraft by demonstrating:

  • Flight-Relevant Integration Readiness: Achieving TRL-6 will validate the system's aerodynamic performance, stability, and reliability. This provides aerospace manufacturers with a highly efficient, drop-in propulsion architecture that reduces OEM R&D and fielding timelines.
  • Leap-Ahead Platform Capabilities: MagLev Aero's technology is designed to unlock step-change improvements in payload capacity, acoustic signature reduction, operational range, and aircraft efficiency—serving as key competitive differentiators for OEMs competing for both future defense and commercial fleet programs.

DARPA EEI - Scaling U.S. Industrialization & Commercialization
Simultaneously, the DARPA EEI Program accelerates MagLev Aero's defense commercialization, go-to-market execution, and U.S. industrialization strategy. The award funds the embedding of an experienced business leader to help navigate federal acquisition frameworks and capture strategic transition opportunities.

  • Capitalizing on "Drone Dominance" Priorities: This executive leadership will strategically position MagLev Aero's capabilities for program capture, large-scale, urgent government procurement efforts across government agencies and armed forces including Air Force, Navy, NASA, AFWERX, U.S. Special Operations Command (USSOCOM), and the Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL).
  • Strengthening Domestic Manufacturing: Driven by the strategic imperative for secure, domestic supply chains, MagLev Aero plans to industrialize a robust, "Made in the U.S." manufacturing and supplier base for industrializing next-generation drone propulsion.

"These dual DARPA contracts represent a major inflection point for MagLev Aero," said Ian Randall, Co-Founder and CEO of MagLev Aero. "We are not just proving out physics in a lab; we are helping build the propulsion industrial base for the next generation of American air power. By rapidly advancing our scalable, domestically manufactured propulsion platform to TRL-6, we are delivering a proven solution that meets the urgent national need for trusted, high-performance U.S. drone technologies."

About MagLev Aero
MagLev Aero is a Boston-based company developing the MagLev HyperDrive™ propulsion platform for the next generation of drones and advanced air vehicles. Backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures and Material Impact, with 44 issued patents, its rim-driven ducted fan architecture leverages its patented MagLev HyperDrive™ technology. The company is devising a new engineering framework combining modern AI compute technology, multiphysics optimization, and human innovation to accelerate electrified propulsion design. The goal: unlock unprecedented levels of efficiency, range, payload, noise reduction, speed, and resiliency, directly enhancing operational capabilities for both defense and commercial aircraft applications.

data.title: Warner Bros. Discovery Announces Intention to Delist Euro Notes from Nasdaq Global
data.description:
Warner Bros. Discovery Announces Intention to Delist Euro Notes from Nasdaq Global

Warner Bros. Discovery Announces Intention to Delist Euro Notes from Nasdaq Global

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Sept. 25, 2026

NEW YORK, Sept. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc. (NASDAQ: WBD) ("WBD" or "Warner Bros. Discovery") today announced that, in connection with the pending acquisition of WBD (the "Acquisition") by Paramount Skydance Corporation ("PSKY"), which is subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions, WBD intends to voluntarily delist from The Nasdaq Global Market ("Nasdaq Global") the 4.302% Senior Notes due 2030 issued by Discovery Global Holdings, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of WBD ("DGH"), and fully and unconditionally guaranteed by WBD and certain of its subsidiaries and the 4.693% Senior Notes due 2033 issued by DGH and fully and unconditionally guaranteed by WBD and certain of its subsidiaries (together, the "Euro Notes"), and to deregister the Euro Notes under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the "Exchange Act").

WBD has decided to take this voluntary action to delist and deregister the Euro Notes because of the pending Acquisition. The voluntary delisting and deregistration of the Euro Notes, if completed, will not affect the terms of the Euro Notes.

To delist the Euro Notes, WBD expects to file a Notification of Removal From Listing on Form 25 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") on or around October 6, 2026. WBD reserves the right to delay the filing of the Form 25 for any reason. The delisting will be effective on the 10th day following filing of the Form 25, and the Euro Notes will no longer trade on Nasdaq Global effective on such date.

Upon effectiveness of the Form 25, WBD expects to file a Certification and Notice of Termination on Form 15 with the SEC with respect to the Euro Notes, requesting that the Euro Notes be deregistered under the Exchange Act, and that the reporting obligations of WBD with respect to the Euro Notes under Sections 13 and 15(d) of the Exchange Act be suspended. Neither WBD nor PSKY have made arrangements for the listing and/or registration of the Euro Notes on another national securities exchange or for quotation on another medium.

Discovery is a leading global media and entertainment company that creates and distributes the world's most differentiated and complete portfolio of branded content across television, film, streaming and gaming. Motion Picture Group, Warner Bros. Television Group, Warner Bros. Pictures Animation, Warner Bros. Games, New Line Cinema, Cartoon Network, Adult Swim, Turner Classic Movies, Discovery en Español, Hogar de HGTV and others.

data.title: DNB Investors Have Opportunity to Lead Dun & Bradstreet Holdings, Inc. Securities Fraud Lawsuit Filed
data.description:
DNB Investors Have Opportunity to Lead Dun & Bradstreet Holdings, Inc. Securities Fraud Lawsuit Filed

DNB Investors Have Opportunity to Lead Dun & Bradstreet Holdings, Inc. Securities Fraud Lawsuit Filed

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Sept. 25, 2026

NEW YORK, Sept. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --

Why: Rosen Law Firm, a global investor rights law firm, reminds persons or entities that: (a) sold shares of Dun & Bradstreet Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: DNB) ("D&B") common stock in the open market from May 13, 2025 through August 26, 2025; (b) exchanged shares of D&B common stock into the August 26, 2025 merger of D&B with affiliates of Clearlake Capital Group, L.P. for $9.15 per share in cash (the "Merger"); and/or (c) held shares of D&B common stock as of the May 9, 2025 Record Date for the special meeting of stockholders and whose shares were voted on, or entitled to vote on, the Merger, of the important November 10, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline.

So What: If you sold Dun & Bradstreet common stock, held shares of D&B common stock on May 9, 2025, or exchanged shares of D&B common stock as a result of its merger, you may be entitled to compensation without payment of any out of pocket fees or costs through a contingency fee arrangement.

What to do next: To join the Dun & Bradstreet class action, go to https://rosenlegal.com/cases/dun-bradstreet-holdings-inc/join or call Phillip Kim, Esq. toll-free at 866-767-3653 or email case@rosenlegal.com for information on the class action. A class action lawsuit has already been filed. If you wish to serve as lead plaintiff, you must move the Court no later than November 10, 2026. A lead plaintiff is a representative party acting on behalf of other class members in directing the litigation.

Why Rosen Law: We encourage investors to select qualified counsel with a track record of success in leadership roles. Often, firms issuing notices do not have comparable experience, resources, or any meaningful peer recognition. Many of these firms do not actually handle securities class actions, but are merely middlemen that refer clients or partner with law firms that actually litigate the cases. Be wise in selecting counsel. The Rosen Law Firm represents investors throughout the globe, concentrating its practice in securities class actions and shareholder derivative litigation. Rosen Law Firm has achieved the largest ever securities class action settlement against a Chinese Company. Rosen Law Firm was Ranked No. 1 by ISS Securities Class Action Services for number of securities class action settlements in 2017. The firm has been ranked in the top 4 each year since 2013 and has recovered billions of dollars for investors. In 2019 alone the firm secured over $438 million for investors. In 2020, founding partner Laurence Rosen was named by law360 as a Titan of Plaintiffs' Bar. Many of the firm's attorneys have been recognized by Lawdragon and Super Lawyers.

Details of the case: The lawsuit seeks to recover damages on behalf of investors that were damaged as a result of allegedly false and misleading statements and omissions of material facts in D&B's March 23, 2025 announcement of the Merger and the May 13, 2025 definitive proxy statement on Schedule 14A (the "Proxy"). Among other things, the complaint alleges the Proxy and other solicitation materials misled investors regarding the true value of the Company and the subject transaction, including portraying the Merger as the product of an ordinary-course strategic review and organic arm's-length interest in D&B, while omitting Executive Chairman Foley's personal interest in a quick sale. The complaint also alleges the Proxy omitted Bank of America Securities' valuations of superior alternatives to a whole-company sale, misstated that D&B's Board of Directors had approved downward revisions to the Company's financial projections and failed to disclose long-standing, material ties between Foley and D&B's financial and legal advisors.

The webcast can be accessed at the following link DAYBREAK Topline Results Webcast or from the Events and Presentations page on Kodiak's website at https://ir.kodiak.com/events-and-presentations/events.

About Kodiak Sciences Inc.

Kodiak Sciences (Nasdaq: KOD) is a pre-commercial retina-focused biotechnology company committed to researching, developing and commercializing transformative therapeutics. We are focused on bringing new science to the design and manufacture of next-generation retinal medicines to prevent and treat the leading causes of blindness globally. We are developing a portfolio of three late-stage clinical programs. Zenkuda™ (tarcocimab tedromer) has a BLA-ready profile in diabetic retinopathy, retinal vein occlusion and wet AMD, and KSI-501 is being evaluated in wet AMD and diabetic macular edema. data.title: Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc. Announces TownBridge Bank as New Name of Bank Subsidiary
data.description:
Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc. Announces TownBridge Bank as New Name of Bank Subsidiary

 New shared bank identity supports Company’s growing Family of Brands while preserving local brands, leadership and relationships

Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc. (OTCQX: MNMB) (the “Company”) today announced that its wholly owned bank subsidiary, Merchants & Marine Bank, will change its legal name to TownBridge Bank, effective September 28, 2026.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260925857654/en/

TownBridge Organization Chart

The name change does not reflect a sale, merger, acquisition, or change in ownership or leadership. Instead, TownBridge Bank establishes a shared bank charter identity for the Company’s growing Family of Brands while allowing its community banking brands to retain the local names, leadership, and relationships they have built within the communities they serve.

Beginning September 28, the Company’s community banking brands will operate as:

  • Merchants & Marine Bank, a division of TownBridge Bank
  • Mississippi River Bank, a division of TownBridge Bank
  • Farmers-Merchants Bank, a division of TownBridge Bank

Beginning September 28, the Company’s ancillary brands will operate as:

  • Canvas Mortgage, a division of TownBridge Bank
  • CannaFirst Financial, a division of TownBridge Bank
  • Voyager Lending, a division of TownBridge Bank

Clients will begin seeing the TownBridge Bank name phased into legal and regulatory references in the days and weeks following the effective date. The Company’s individual brands will otherwise continue operating as they do today, and clients can expect to see the same familiar brands, locations, bankers, and local leadership teams they know and trust.

“TownBridge represents an important next step in the evolution of our company, but it doesn’t change who we are or how we serve our communities,” said Clayton Legear, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc. & TownBridge Bank. “We believe deeply in hometowns, small towns and Main Streets, and in the value of local bankers who know the people, businesses and communities they serve. TownBridge gives our Family of Brands a clearer common identity and a stronger foundation from which to continue growing.”

Historically, Merchants & Marine Bank has served two roles within the organization: as a local community banking brand in its Mississippi and Alabama markets, and as the legal bank charter supporting the Company’s other banking brands. As the Company has expanded its Family of Brands across multiple markets and multiple states, TownBridge creates a neutral shared charter identity that allows each community banking brand to operate equally as a division of TownBridge Bank.

The TownBridge name also reflects the Company’s longstanding community banking focus and philosophy. “Town” honors the hometowns and communities the Company’s brands serve and carries forward the ethos behind Merchants & Marine Bank’s longtime identity as “Hometown People That You Know.” “Bridge” represents the connections community bankers build among families, businesses, capital, opportunity, and the communities around them.

“Great community banks are deeply connected to the places they call home, and we believe that is something worth preserving,” Legear continued. “Our goal is to build a different kind of community banking company – one that combines the strength, resources and expertise of a larger organization with the local leadership, local decision-making, relationships and community focus that make great community banks special. TownBridge gives us an identity built to carry this model into the future; strengthening the communities we serve today while creating opportunities to serve new communities in the years ahead.”

TownBridge Bank will continue to be governed by the bank charter’s existing Board of Directors and led by the existing Corporate Executive Leadership Team that has overseen the Company’s sustained growth and development of its Family of Brands strategy. The Company’s ownership structure is unchanged, and Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc. will remain the parent company of TownBridge Bank.

As a next step, the Company intends to seek shareholder approval at its 2027 Annual Meeting of Shareholders to align the Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc. name with the TownBridge identity, subject to applicable requirements.

The TownBridge Bank name change itself will not require clients to take any action or change how they bank with the Company’s brands. Account and routing numbers will not change as a result of the name change, and clients may continue using their existing checks, cards, brand websites, and digital banking access as they do today.

Additional information about TownBridge Bank is available at TownBridge.bank.

About Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc.

Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc. (OTCQX: MNMB) is the parent company of TownBridge Bank, a Mississippi chartered community bank serving the Gulf South region. TownBridge Bank was originally founded as Merchants & Marine Bank in 1899, and the bank was reborn in 1932 during the middle of the worst economic disaster in the history of the United States: The Great Depression.

The Bank offers banking services to customers in Southern Mississippi and Coastal Alabama under its legacy Merchants & Marine Bank brand, in Southeastern Louisiana through its Mississippi River Bank brand, and in the Acadiana Region of Louisiana through its Farmers-Merchants Bank brand. It offers mortgage financing through its Canvas Mortgage brand, cannabis banking through its CannaFirst Financial brand, and access to government-guaranteed credit through its Voyager Lending brand. It provides bank operational, risk, and support services through its Community of Resources bank services brand.

data.title: A 'death cross' is coming for the dollar. Why Trump will be happy.
data.description:
By Tomi Kilgore

The moving-average crossover to the downside isn't the only chart signal to suggest the uptrend is reversing - and that government intervention may have actually worked

A "death cross" looks set to appear in the chart of the dollar-yen rate, suggesting the long-term uptrend is reversing.

Don't look now, but there are some technical reasons to believe that U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was right when he declared to the financial markets that "I am the house now."

Not only has the upside momentum apparently swung to the Japanese yen , and away from its U.S. dollar counterpart, but a chart pattern ominously known as a "death cross" is developing - it's likely to be confirmed early next week - that suggests the rapid uptrend in the dollar-yen rate, which threatened Japan's economy and is unwanted by the Trump administration, may have actually reversed.

Death crosses aren't necessarily good market-timing signals, but they help reinforce the idea that a new trend may have started. "We like to say that every major downside move starts with a death cross, but not every death cross leads to a major decline," wrote Ari Wald, head of technical analysis at Oppenheimer & Co., in emailed comments to MarketWatch.

On Friday, the dollar-yen rate (USDJPY) dropped 1% in afternoon trading toward its biggest one-day decline in three weeks - with Bessent posting on X about President Trump's endorsement of the "desirability of a strong yen," which the Bank of Japan has been pushing for. The selloff came at the right time on the charts to provide further evidence that the 17-month-long uptrend may have been broken. As the yen strengthens against the dollar, the dollar-yen rate declines.

When the government tells investors to stop buying something, there can be an almost defiant interest to do just the opposite, as it can suggest the powers that be have reason to believe the rally will continue unless they intervene directly in the market to stop it.

And history is littered with examples of when government intervention has failed, even spectacularly, to stop the markets - such as the collapse of the British pound (GBPUSD) in 1992 and the Asian financial crisis of the late 1990s, as well as Bessent's recent attempts to slow the rise in longer-term Treasury yields.

So when the U.S. Treasury collaborated with the Bank of Japan to halt the continued climb in the dollar-yen exchange rate in late July, many believed that while the rate might fall initially, the fundamentals that brought it to that level would kick back in and the price would soon resume its path.

But after a brief bout of strength, the currency pair broke on Sept. 3 below a trend line that tracked the rally off the April 2025 lows. Buyers once again stepped in and the rate rose back up to test the trend line, to see if it was really broken. Friday's selloff confirmed that it was.

And the selloff comes right after dollar-yen rate tried to get back above the 200-day moving average, which many chart watchers view as a dividing line between longer-term uptrends and downtrends.

"Today's failure at the 200-day moving average leaves the [currency] pair vulnerable to a test of 152 support, near the 2026 lows," Wald wrote.

Next comes the death cross.

That pattern appears when the 50-day moving average, a widely followed short-term trend tracker, crosses below the 200-DMA. That is seen as marking the spot where a shorter-term decline graduates to a longer-term downtrend.

Based on the current trajectories of dollar-yen's 50-DMA and 200-DMA, the crossover should occur before the end of next week. That would mark the first death cross for the currency pair since March 25, 2025.

After that appearance, prices fell another 6% before bottoming about a month later.

But the death cross before that had appeared on Sept. 9, 2024, and prices bottomed a week later after just another 1.8% decline.

Still, Oppenheimer's Wald believes that in the current technical setup, the death cross "aligns with a broad loss of momentum," and it "strengthens the case for a trend reversal."

-Tomi Kilgore

data.title: 'She says it's just money': My friend pays for everything. I should be grateful, but I can't stand her anymore.
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'On each of these weekends away, she's probably spending $500'

"She isn't a bad person - in fact, she's kind and generous. But she can be exhausting." (Photo subjects are models.)

Dear Quentin,

I am 56 and have a confession that makes me feel like a terrible person: I have a friend, 58, who likes me much more than I like her. It feels harsh to say it. She doesn't have that many friends, so I feel like I'm doing her a kindness. But she can be draining and very negative.

We've known each other for 20 years. We're both married with kids. She's always been generous - maybe too generous - considerably better off than I am, and she regularly takes me out to expensive restaurants. If I offer to pay my share, she waves me off.

Of late, her generosity has gone further. She has invited me on weekend trips and covered the hotel. I try, in turn, to pay for dinner. She says she enjoys having someone to travel with, and I've accepted, because frankly I couldn't afford to do these things as often on my own.

The problem is that I don't particularly enjoy spending time with her. She isn't a bad person - in fact, she's kind and generous. But she can be exhausting. She talks almost exclusively about herself, interrupts constantly and has an opinion about everyone, often an unflattering one.

I've noticed I'm often relieved when our weekend is over. That makes me feel guilty, because she has been so good to me. But on each of these trips, she's probably spending $500, and we've taken quite a few of them over the years. She says it's just money.

I've noticed I'm often relieved when our weekend is over. That makes me feel guilty.

I also know she considers me a close friend. She tells other people how much she enjoys our friendship, and talks about future trips we could take together. I don't feel the same way. I like her well enough, but I don't look forward to seeing her the way I do my closest friends.

I've tried to reciprocate in smaller ways - buying dinner, bringing wine when we're staying somewhere, picking up other expenses. But I could never match what she spends on me. Also, she can be quite mean about others, and she turns every topic of conversation back to herself.

Recently, she invited me on another weekend away. I found myself hoping she'd cancel. That's when I realized something uncomfortable: I may be continuing this friendship partly because I like to get away from my husband and kids, but also because I'm too scared to end it.

I've never asked her to pay for anything. She's an adult who can afford these trips. But I also know that if I told her honestly that I didn't want to spend so much time together, she'd be hurt. How do I essentially end a friendship that has lasted decades with someone I no longer like?

Should I tell her I don't consider us as close as she does? Or would that be unnecessarily cruel? I don't want her weekends away. I'm not sure if I really ever did. But I don't want to pretend I value the friendship more than I do, simply because she's generous.

A Friend, Apparently

Related: My golf buddy worked as a financial adviser. Here's how I knew his friendship was fake.

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Boundaries are extremely tricky to maintain with people who are insistent and/or bordering on pushy.

Dear Apparently,

You owe it to both of you to end this friendship. It's no longer serving anyone.

I don't blame you for finding yourself in this situation. Boundaries are extremely tricky to maintain with people who are insistent and/or bordering on pushy. They're even more difficult to maintain when someone comes offering a friendly ear, at first, and gifts.

There are two types of friendship: healthy friendships and unhealthy friendships, but no friendship is perfect, and it can sometimes be difficult to tell the difference between the two. Money, as this column can attest to, makes that even more complicated.

And there are two kinds of toxic friendships: one that is transactional and one that is based in trauma. They can overlap, of course, but these are to be avoided. As you get older, we should all be more self contained and have less need for a "best friend" outside of our spouse.

There are two kinds of toxic friendships: transactional and trauma-based.

If you each take turns listening to each other's problems ad nauseum, no one wins. It's codependent and negative. If one person is offering gifts or another person seeks social connections, that's when a friendship can become transactional.

It can be all too easy to conflate generosity of spirit with financial largesse. The former comes without a price. The latter often has a gift tax attached. There's a price to be paid: you lend an ear, you overlook a harsh word and, yes, you ultimately hand over your time.

There comes a time, as we get older, that we realize our time is the most precious commodity, more than gold, real estate, equities, bonds, designer clothing, vacation homes, 401(k)s, IRAs, money-market funds, you name it. Honoring that realization requires hard decisions.

Related: 'It feels slimy': My friend offered to be my adviser, but didn't tell me he's paid to push financial products. Can I trust him?

Ending a friendship

These weekends felt harmless at first and, perhaps you paid your way by taking care of dinners, which could almost cost as much as $500 over the course of two days. But you are still put under an obligation, and these gifts create an intangible, everpresent debt to be repaid.

This would be less of an issue if you actually liked this friend as much as she appears to like - or want to be friends with - you. That's the real crux. We can analyze the nature of financial and emotional inequity all day, but it's time to honor both parties and take action.

You may need to do one or two things: (1.) Start saying no to invitations. If this friend doesn't step back in an organic manner - and I have a feeling she won't go quietly - you need to (2.) Tell her that you need space, and you have a lot going on in your life.

These gifts create an intangible, everpresent debt to be repaid.

If need be, you can meet in person and tell her the truth - you don't have the time to devote to the friendship and, if she asks, you can tell her it's you not her, and if she pushes, you feel like she wants more from the friendship than you feel like you can give.

Here's the thing: You're not exiting a relationship or a marriage, you are extricating yourself from a friendship that doesn't serve you and, honestly, it doesn't serve your friend either if you really don't like her as much as you should to sustain a friendship.

Having to be less than yourself when you are with her and essentially act like you are having a better time, or not feel like you can fully relax and be your most authentic self, will cost you more than the price of a weekend away. It will be a constant intrusion in your life.

Boundaries are free to build, but they take work - and they are a daily practice.

Don't miss: Why does almost nobody want to befriend older people like me - except scammers?

data.title: Utilities Shares Tick Higher as Energy Rally Cools — Utilities Roundup
data.description:
Shares of utility companies pared weekly losses as energy costs stabilized around elevated levels and the rapid rise in Treasury yields cooled a bit.

Oil prices fell as investors assessed prospects for U.S.-Iran diplomacy aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, U.S. natural-gas futures pared gains that were due to the outage on a pipeline in West Virginia operated by a unit of TC Energy.

While no date for a resumption of service had been given, the fact the problem was confined to the regulator station "reduced concern that the outage will require a prolonged pipeline-integrity response," Gelber & Associates said in a note. LNG feedgas flows continue to support market balances, "but cooling demand is declining as the market moves deeper into the shoulder season," the firm added.
